name: c3bot-relay-go
description: Go port of c3bot-relay (Telegram <-> c3 relay: WebSocket /ws, SSE /events, long-poll /poll, POST /send, /claim lease, webhook + getUpdates failover), shadow stage: runs next to the Node container on its own port, own container and own state, with ephemeral secrets and no Telegram access, outside every request path (ticket #1873)

native_build._doc: Multi-stage: compiled in golang:1.24-bookworm on the arch-matched runner (oci-apps is arm64), shipped as one static binary on distroless static (no shell, no libc, non-root 65532; unlike bare scratch it carries the CA bundle the Telegram TLS calls need). Same template as infra-sec_introspect-proxy-go.

api.description: Same contract as c3bot-relay: WS /ws, SSE /events, long-poll /poll, POST /send, /claim and /release lease, POST /webhook, GET /health. Shadow stage: ephemeral bearer, no Telegram.

parity-compare._doc: Reference = the Node relay (infra-ops_c3bot-relay/src/code/server.js) run under node with its own throwaway token and a fake Telegram API; the same request sequences go to both and the transcripts must be identical. See parity/parity_test.go.

_doc_shadow: Shadow stage (#1873). The live Node relay (container c3bot-relay, port 3119, its own vault secrets) is untouched. This container has NO env_file and mounts no secret: SHADOW_EPHEMERAL=1 makes the process generate a random bearer and webhook secret at start and ignore any bot token, so it cannot read or acknowledge the live queue, cannot post to Telegram and cannot claim a lease on the live relay; nothing outside the process can call its API. It logs a periodic `shadow-selfcheck PASS|FAIL` of its own contract. State lives on a tmpfs (/state, uid 65532): the Ship's generated Dockerfile cannot pre-create a writable volume dir for the nonroot user, and the persistence logic is covered by the Go tests and the parity run.
_doc_addressing: No mesh name, no Caddy route and no client wiring on purpose during the shadow stage: only the container itself dials its bind address (10.0.0.6:3129, oci-apps WG IP), so it needs no Hickory row and no Caddy fallback-map entry. Switch-over (real secrets, mesh name, route) is a separate step after the shadow has run clean.
